strings.name: Carlos Slim
strings.summary: Carlos Slim began in securities, property and industrial investment, acquired companies during Mexico’s debt crisis and entered telecommunications through the privatization of Telmex. Family-linked businesses expanded through América Móvil across Latin America and other markets, alongside retail, infrastructure and finance. His scale of investment and philanthropy is accompanied by continuing questions about telecom market power and competition regulation.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 13 November 2026; selected events reach May 2026, with a September 2026 public-event caption also corroborating living status. Slim, his family and companies are distinguished; a market-dominance designation is not described as a personal criminal judgment.
strings.influence.rationale: Developed telecommunications and industrial businesses across the Americas, influencing infrastructure, finance and communications markets in Mexico.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Civil engineering, National Autonomous University of Mexico (completed in 1961)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Expanding Latin American telecommunications
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Participated in Telmex’s 1990 privatization and later expanded multinational fixed and mobile communications through América Móvil.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Allocating capital across industries
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Expanded from finance and property into manufacturing, retail and infrastructure, using acquisitions during downturns as an important route of growth.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Questions a deepwater gas project
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Publicly described the Lakach project linked to Pemex as irrational, highlighting questions about the feasibility of an energy investment.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Telecom businesses face stronger regulation
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Mexico’s regulator designated América Móvil as dominant, subjecting it to stricter competition measures.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: América Móvil is spun off
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Telmex spun off mobile operations in Mexico and other countries, creating a platform for international telecom expansion.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Participates in the Telmex acquisition
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Joined Southwestern Bell and France Telecom in the privatization, making telecommunications a central part of his business interests.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Establishes a philanthropic foundation
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Created the Carlos Slim Foundation to support education, health and social programs.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Invests during Mexico’s debt crisis
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Continued acquiring industrial and retail businesses during Mexico’s economic and financial crisis, broadening his holdings.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Forms a diversified industrial group
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Formed Grupo Galas, later Grupo Carso, with interests in industry, construction, retail and food.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Begins securities and property businesses
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Established Inversora Bursátil and developed Carso property interests, laying foundations for later investments.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Completes civil engineering studies
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Finished professional studies at UNAM, where he also taught mathematics-related courses while studying.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Mexico City
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Mexico City, where he later based much of his investment and business activity.
